title: Monash Academic Salary: Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay Under the 38-Hour Week
description: Learn how to convert a Monash academic salary from hourly to annual using the 38-hour week, award rates, casual loading, and super. Fair Work Ombudsman rates included.
salarySummary: For a Monash academic at Level A1, the annual salary is $68,991 based on 38 hours per week at $34.80 per hour, with super paid on top.

faqs.q: How do I calculate annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then by 52. For a standard full-time role under the Higher Education Industry–Academic Staff Award 2020, ordinary hours are 38 per week. So annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, a Level A1 academic at $34.80 per hour earns $68,991 per year. This matches the Fair Work Ombudsman pay guide. Remember that this formula assumes consistent hours and no unpaid overtime.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading for academic staff under the award?
faqs.a: Casual academics receive a 25% loading on the minimum hourly rate, as per clause 12.1 of the award. However, the award also sets specific flat rates for lecturing, tutoring, and marking that already include the casual loading. For example, a basic lecture (1 hour delivery plus 2 hours associated work) pays $173.99 per hour of delivery. Do not add the 25% loading on top of these flat rates. For other casual work not covered by those specific rates, the loading applies to the base hourly rate.

faqs.q: How does superannuation affect my take-home pay?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your gross salary. Under the award, employers must contribute at least the super guarantee rate (12% from 1 July 2026) of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a Monash academic on $68,991, the super contribution would be about $8,279 per year, added to your super fund, not to your take-home pay. Your take-home pay is your gross salary minus tax and Medicare levy. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for an estimate.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the 38-Hour Week and Annual Conversion

When you hear about a **Monash academic salary**, the first step is to understand how hourly rates translate into annual figures. The standard full-time working week under the *Higher Education Industry–Academic Staff Award 2020* is 38 hours. To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, use the formula:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For example, a Level A1 academic (the entry-level classification) earns a minimum hourly rate of $34.80. Multiply by 38 hours and 52 weeks: $34.80 × 38 × 52 = $68,991 per year. This matches the rate published by the Fair Work Ombudsman in the pay guide for the award.

This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It is a starting point for comparing offers or understanding your base pay.

### Fortnightly Pay

Most Australian universities pay staff fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, divide the annual salary by 26 (52 weeks ÷ 2). For a Level A1 academic, that is $68,991 ÷ 26 = $2,653.50 per fortnight before tax. Alternatively, multiply your weekly pay by 2: weekly pay = $34.80 × 38 = $1,322.40, so fortnightly = $2,644.80 (slight rounding difference due to the award’s calculation method).

## Monash Academic Salary Under the Award

Monash University’s enterprise agreement adopts the award rates as a minimum. The Fair Work Commission’s consolidated award lists the following annual salaries and hourly rates for full-time teaching and research academics (non-medical/dental):

| Classification | Annual Salary | Hourly Rate |
|----------------|---------------|-------------|
| Level A1 | $68,991 | $34.80 |
| Level A6 | $81,432 | $41.08 |
| Level B1 | $89,382 | $45.09 |
| Level C1 | $104,940 | $52.94 |
| Level D1 | $122,225 | $61.66 |
| Level E | $151,614 | $76.48 |

These rates apply from the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026. If you are negotiating a **Monash academic salary**, check whether your offer is above these minimums. The award also includes clinical loadings for medical and dental academics, ranging from $15,178 to $30,287 per year depending on the department.

### Casual Academic Rates

Casual academics are paid under clause 16.4 of the award. The rates are flat and include the 25% casual loading. For example:
- Basic lecture (1 hour delivery + 2 hours associated work): $173.99 per hour of delivery
- Tutorial (1 hour + 2 hours associated): $135.76 per hour
- Standard marking: $45.22 per hour

These rates are higher than the base hourly rate plus loading because they incorporate associated working time. If you hold a relevant doctoral qualification, you receive a higher rate (e.g., tutorial $154.09 per hour).

## Casual Loading and Superannuation

For casual employees not covered by the specific flat rates, the award requires a 25% loading on the minimum hourly rate. For example, a casual Level A1 academic doing general work would earn $34.80 + 25% = $43.50 per hour. However, the award’s specific rates (lecturing, tutoring, marking) already include that loading, so you should not add it again.

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a full-time academic on $68,991, the employer contributes an extra $8,279 per year to your super fund. This is not part of your take-home pay but is a valuable benefit. Use the [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) guide to understand salary sacrifice options.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). Casual employees get a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. Award rates for academics are significantly higher, reflecting the skill and qualifications required. Always check the relevant award or enterprise agreement before accepting a role.

## Fortnightly Pay and Tax Considerations

Your take-home pay depends on tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 income year, the resident tax rates are:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,370 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. For a Level A1 academic earning $68,991, the estimated tax is about $10,617 plus Medicare $1,380, leaving a take-home of about $56,994 per year, or $2,192 per fortnight. These are estimates; use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a personalised result.

### Using the Timesheet Tool

Our [timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add the 25% casual loading. It then shows your annual, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. Remember: if you are on a casual academic rate that already includes loading (like the flat lecture rates), do not check the casual loading box.

## Summary

Converting a **Monash academic salary** from hourly to annual is straightforward: multiply by 38 hours and 52 weeks. The award sets minimum rates that increase with classification and experience. Casual academics have specific flat rates that include loading. Super is paid on top, and tax reduces your take-home. Always refer to the [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data) for the most current figures.
